**Recovering Split PDF page-tree roots (2026-11-01):** Fixed the Split flow for PDFs whose catalog `/Pages` root has `/Kids` and `/Count` but omits `/Type /Pages`. This input loaded in `pdf-lib` but `getPageCount()` threw `_this.catalog.Pages(...).traverse is not a function`; PDF.js recognized 911 pages. Split now restores the missing root type only after validating the tree shape and child nodes. The same local file then reports 911 pages without extracting content or generating a copy. A synthetic one-page regression verifies recovery, copy, save, and reload. `npm.cmd test` passes 99/99; `npm.cmd run build` succeeds with existing `buffer` externalization and large-chunk warnings; `git diff --check` passes. Actual page extraction/download from the supplied book was not performed.

The category tabs replace the old dropdowns with direct icon-and-label links, identify the active category on category pages and tool routes, and use a blue underline and subtle hover tint. At a requested 360 px viewport, the tab bar fit five links without internal overflow; detailed measurement is in the checklist. `npm.cmd run build` and `git diff --check` passed after this change; the existing `buffer` externalization and large-chunk warnings remain. Animated hero badges retain their existing homepage-section links. Shared category navigation, homepage cards with a bottom-up blue hover/focus tint, category-aware search, related tools, and persisted light/dark theme are implemented. The homepage hero has a two-column message and an animated PDF illustration with five interactive, registry-driven category links; hover/focus pauses and enlarges a badge, and reduced-motion preferences disable rotation. Desktop animation, geometry, interactions, and themes are browser-verified. A mobile screenshot exposed clipped orbit labels; small-screen radius and label sizing were tightened, but post-fix mobile verification is pending because the browser reported a 982 px layout viewport after a 390 px resize request. The npm manifest now identifies the application accurately; its lockfile includes the approved exact `@pdfsmaller/pdf-decrypt@1.0.1` dependency without unrelated upgrades. The three direct `@types/*` development packages may be unnecessary because there are no TypeScript sources or type-check script; they were retained pending confirmation that they are not wanted for editor support. There are no lint or test scripts. Empty categories are omitted from navigation and the homepage. Ordinary PDF tools reject password-protected inputs before adding them to selected-file state; the dedicated Unlock PDF route is the authorized-password exception. Unlock PDF is registered at `/unlock` under Protect & Repair and processes locally, accepting only supported AES-256 R6/RC4 R2/R3 encryption when a correct password is supplied. Synthetic AES-256 and RC4 browser flows, wrong-password rejection, unencrypted/invalid-file rejection, page-count preservation, and password-free output parsing were verified. Browser download-event capture remains unverified. Merge PDF accepts at most five files and disables upload at the limit. Excel/PowerPoint conversion routes deliberately explain the missing local renderer rather than accepting files or pretending to convert them. PDF-to-Word and OCR PDF may fetch OCR resources from jsDelivr. The shared tool-detail hero has a category/icon/title/summary area and a separate, readable overview panel; it was browser-checked on all 16 tool routes and both Office limitation routes.

## Unlock PDF implementation — 2026-10-29
- Added the user-approved exact runtime dependency `@pdfsmaller/pdf-decrypt@1.0.1` (MIT, `pdf-lib` peer dependency) and synchronized `package-lock.json`; no unrelated package versions changed. Reviewed its published browser entry point and confirmed the implementation uses Web Crypto and PDF object parsing without a document-upload/network call. The package supports AES-256 R6 and RC4 R2/R3; AES-128 R4 is explicitly unsupported.
- Implemented `/unlock` with a separate component and registry entry under Protect & Repair. It accepts only detected encrypted PDFs, requires a user-supplied password, clears the password from UI state after each attempt, and has explicit wrong-password/unsupported/unencrypted/invalid-file messages. It does not modify the shared validator or other tools' encrypted-input rejection.
- The component decrypts in-browser, independently opens the source with PDF.js using the supplied password to count pages, then loads the output with `pdf-lib` without a password and verifies the output is unencrypted and retains the source page count. It provides a separate manual download and warns users to review signatures, forms, annotations, attachments, and specialized features because the PDF is rewritten.

The Protect & Repair category listed all three tools, search surfaced Unlock PDF and opened `/unlock`, and neutral info/status surfaces computed correctly in both light and dark themes. Browser download-event capture was attempted but not observed, so the final download action remains unverified.

## Watermark PDF — 2026-10-28
- Added `src/components/PdfWatermarker.jsx`, registered `/watermark` in `src/App.jsx`, and added an active matching homepage card in `src/components/Home.jsx`.
- Uses installed `pdf-lib` APIs (`drawText`, `StandardFonts.Helvetica`, `rgb`, `degrees`, and text opacity) to add centered, rotated text without rasterizing pages or changing the source file.
- Supports text, 8–96 pt size, colour, -180° to 180° rotation, 0–100% opacity, all pages, and strict 1-based page/range selection.
- Also supports independent page numbering with starting number, top/bottom placement, alignment, colour, size, margin, and an independent page range.
- Displays file size and loaded page count; supports replacing, removing, and resetting the selected file. Output page count and order are retained.
- Limitations: built-in Helvetica has WinAnsi character coverage, so unsupported text is rejected; password-protected PDFs are not supported.

Category menu pointer and keyboard focus behavior and homepage card Tab/Enter activation were verified. Physical keyboard hardware behavior remains unverified in this headless browser.

On Remove PDF Pages at 360/768/1280px, a 50-page PDF produced all 50 previews with no horizontal overflow. A 51-page PDF was rejected with an explicit limit message.

- Extract PDF Pages: selected pages in order 3 then 1; generated output parsed as two pages in source order (`TEST PAGE 1`, `TEST PAGE 3`).
- Watermark numbering: numbering-only mode with start 7 and selected pages 1,3 generated three pages; extracted text showed 7 on page 1, no number on page 2, and 8 on page 3. Text watermark mode with range 2-3 generated text on only those pages and preserved original text. Oversized text on a small synthetic page was rejected.

- Browser inspections captured generated PDF blobs and reopened them with PDF.js to verify page count/order/text. A real browser download event was not captured; watermark appearance was not visually inspected. Do not claim visual verification.
- Organize PDF: generated from a three-page synthetic source after moving page 2 first, rotating it 90 degrees, and removing page 3. PDF.js verified a two-page output in source order 2 then 1, with source text retained and page 1 rotated 90 degrees.
- Redact PDF: generated from a three-page synthetic source with a drag-drawn mask. PDF.js verified three pages and empty text extraction on all pages; sampled mask pixel was black `[0,0,0]`, and unmasked source-text pixels remained visible. This confirms content removal via rasterization for the test fixture, not general visual fidelity.
- Sign PDF: typed signature output retained original text and placed the mark only on selected pages 2-3. Drawn and uploaded-PNG modes produced image-paint operations while preserving source text. Reversed (`3-1`) and out-of-range (`4` for three pages) selections were rejected; Reset cleared the file and alert.

Category navigation opened `/redact`; menu dismissal and mobile category switching also worked.

- Generated Organize, Redact, and Sign output Blobs were reopened and parsed with PDF.js. Browser download events for these new tools were not captured, so an actual saved download remains unverified.
- Browser verified the Watermark card navigates to `/watermark`, a synthetic three-page PDF's filename/size/page count, invalid out-of-range selection rejection, selected/all processing states, replacement picker, and reset.
- Earlier Node/PDF.js verification reopened generated watermarked PDFs, retained four pages and original text, and extracted watermarks only on selected pages or all pages as requested. The test exercised colour, rotation, and opacity.
